My wife and I are selling her 2012 Toyota Camry Hybrid XLE, currently with 145,010 miles at time of this post. It is a clean title, title in hand, with active registration in excellent mechanical condition with regular service history, oil changes every 5,000-7,500 miles, and a recent (late August) multi-point inspection confirming everything is in good shape. Tires have good tread depth, most recently rotated by Les Schwab earlier this year. I have the auto service report and inspection results from Integrity Automotive in Issaquah dated 8/24/26, and I am happy to provide the PDF on request. The tire pressure indicator sensors are broken (classic with every Toyota of this generation), so the TPMS light is always on despite appropriate tire pressure. The hybrid battery is in good shape, it typically averages 38-42 MPG depending on the driving conditions. Photos of the car have had their backgrounds blurred for privacy. The XLE trim means it is fully loaded with features including heated front seats, push-to-start, keyless entry, power moon roof, power front seats, blind spot monitor indicator lights, etc. It is a very quiet, comfy ride. It has no accident history, but 3 instances of cosmetic damage on the right side from separate events. 1) The passenger side back door cosmetic damage is from an underground parking garage wall, making too tight of a turn and scraping on the wall. 2) The passenger side view mirror cosmetic damage is from backing out of a garage and hitting the garage door track. The mirror still folds in and out, the glass itself is not damaged, the defrosters still work, and the blind spot monitoring still works no problem. The damage is purely cosmetic. 3) The passenger side front bumper is sagging, but this was not from any particular event. The plastic clips that hold it up have worn with age, and we paid a Toyota dealership to fix it back in 2021. Unfortunately, a year later the bumper began to sag on that side again. We looked under the car and found they had “fixed” the bumper by securing it with zipties, but we were charged for a brand new bumper and new clips. We took it back to Toyota and told them/showed them, and they denied everything, saying it must have been another shop (they were the only shop we went to), and they would not re-do their work or refund us. So, we have elected to just leave it as is and have not re-attempted to get it fixed since. It doesn’t hang low enough to impede driving, and has not gotten any worse in the 4 years since. The vehicle is my wife’s daily driver and will continue to be driven until sold, so mileage will be higher at time of sale. My wife is the second owner since 2018, she purchased it from her grandmother who also had it regularly serviced. We are selling because her grandmother is no longer able to drive, so we will be purchasing her grandmother’s newer car. As such, we’re not in a particular rush to sell and are willing to negotiate, but we will not take excessively low offers. Payment is accepted in cash, or a cashiers check if you are willing to meet us at your bank so we can see the cashiers check ordered and handed to us directly from the teller. We will not accept a personal check, money order, or Venmo/Zelle/CashApp. We’d be happy to let you test drive as long as you show us your valid drivers license. If you have any questions please feel free to reach out, and I would be happy to answer them.
